reason: An AI writing a script about my anxiety and reading it back to me in a synthetic voice is exactly what I don't want. YouTube has real people doing this for free and I already use it before deadlines.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube for this, and I don't trust AI with anything about my head.
would_change_my_mind: A friend I trust telling me it actually helped them, plus knowing a real clinician or meditation teacher wrote what the AI works from.

v1.why: Opens on someone else's chat and a coin counter; feels like a gimmicky AI toy.

v2.why: Nicer start but still an AI deciding what my stress needs.

v3.why: The 'Why?' on suggestions is the only thing that eases the trust issue, not enough to stay.

reason: I'd try it because it's free and the 'make it about tonight' idea is new. But I paid for Calm and stopped after a month, and the free tier gives me enough to see whether I even keep opening it.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube for this; I proved to myself I don't stick with paid ones.
would_change_my_mind: If my Oura sleep score actually went up on nights I used it, and it showed me that, I'd pay.

v1.why: Percentages that are made up next to my real sleep score would annoy me.

v2.why: Better flow, but nothing that ties into the sleep data I already check every morning.

v3.why: Wearable link is the one hook that matches my morning habit; I'd keep the free tier.

reason: My therapist suggests stuff between sessions and a personalised wind-down sounds genuinely useful, so I'd try it. But therapy already eats my budget, and $10 a month on top needs proof first.
objection: Will it actually help, or is it a gimmick? A minute-made script isn't therapy.
would_change_my_mind: A few weeks of noticeably better sleep scores, or my therapist saying it's a reasonable tool.

v1.why: '24%, needs improvement' with a red arrow is the opposite of what I need on a bad day.

v2.why: Asking 'how do you feel now?' after listening feels closer to how my therapist works.

v3.why: Progress in words and a private journal fit how I already think about this.

reason: The chips and the mic button mean I might not have to type much, so I'd poke at it once or twice. I've never paid for a meditation app and a free YouTube rain video does the job.
objection: I don't want to type how I feel when I already feel bad, and every screen seems to want words from me.
would_change_my_mind: One-tap sessions that are clearly better than my free ones, without the questions.

v1.why: A check-in form with notes the moment I sign in is exactly what I'd close.

v2.why: Three skippable questions are fine, but I'd drift back to YouTube.

v3.why: Least pushy of the three, journal is optional, but still not worth leaving free apps.

reason: That hour after the kids go down is mine, and I'd test it there once or twice. Headspace didn't stick for me and I'm not convinced a custom script beats any decent wind-down track.
objection: Will it actually help, or is it a gimmick? Personalised sounds like marketing.
would_change_my_mind: If after two weeks I could honestly say I fall asleep faster, I'd pay the yearly price.

v1.why: Coins and a hamburger menu make it feel like a game, not a tool.

v2.why: Simple tabs, my own first session, chapter 2 tomorrow gives me a reason to come back.

v3.why: Same as v2 with extras I wouldn't use; fine but not needed.

reason: I don't want a chatbot improvising mental health content, and 'Aurelia AI can make mistakes' at the bottom of a calming session says it all. Before a big meeting I'd rather do a breathing exercise I know works.
objection: Will it actually help, or is it a gimmick? It reads like AI wrapped around a meditation app.
would_change_my_mind: Evidence, even a small study, that these sessions reduce stress, and clarity about who reviews the scripts.

v1.why: Made-up analytics and someone else's chat look like a demo, not a product.

v2.why: Cleaner, still AI-generated content I don't trust.

v3.why: The 'Why?' is a good sign but doesn't fix my distrust.

reason: Forty minutes with headphones twice a day is a real slot, so I'd try it on the train. But it's a browser app with no phone app yet, and I cancelled Calm because I stopped opening it.
objection: Another subscription I'll forget to use, and a web app is easy to forget on a commute.
would_change_my_mind: A proper phone app with offline downloads I can queue up for the commute.

v1.why: Too much going on before I get to the audio.

v2.why: Tabs and a straight path to my session suit a quick commute open.

v3.why: Fine, but journal and reports are more things I won't keep up.

reason: I'd sign up once out of curiosity because it's free. I've never paid for one of these and $10 a month for something YouTube does free isn't happening.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube for this.
would_change_my_mind: Nothing at $10; maybe if it were a couple of dollars or bundled with something I already pay for.

v1.why: Coin balance everywhere makes me think it's going to nickel-and-dime me.

v2.why: Pleasant, but I'd forget it within a week.

v3.why: Best looking, still no reason to switch from free.

reason: Something made for how I feel that morning could fit my commute, so I'd try it. I left Headspace partly because it nagged me, and this looks like it wants a check-in every day.
objection: I don't want an app asking me questions every day.
would_change_my_mind: If I could switch the check-ins off completely and it still adapted, I'd consider paying.

v1.why: A daily check-in sheet popping up on sign-in is my exact complaint.

v2.why: Onboarding questions plus 'how do you feel now?' after each session is still a lot of asking.

v3.why: Wearable could replace some questions, but it's off by default and I'd still churn.

reason: I try every new wellness AI app and this one actually does something different: a session built for today, fresh for my commute. $10 is nothing next to what I already spend, so I'd pay to get longer sessions and every voice.
objection: I don't want an app asking me questions every day; I want it to read my Whoop and just know.

v1.why: Fake analytics and a check-in form feel like an unfinished prototype.

v2.why: Solid flow and the chapter structure gives me a reason to return.

v3.why: Wearable link and a 'Why?' on changes are what I'd want; I'd turn the wearable on day one.
